content.value_statement: React TypeScript work often needs precise event, hook, and route types. This skill provides focused patterns for typed components, React 19 APIs, and routing.
actual_capabilities: Provides TypeScript patterns for React props, children, refs, and discriminated unions.
Shows typed event handlers for mouse, form, input, keyboard, clipboard, and related events.
Explains React 19 patterns including ref as prop, useActionState, use(), and Server Components.
Includes generic component examples for tables, selects, lists, form fields, and modals.
Documents type-safe routing with TanStack Router and React Router v7.
Shows typed hooks patterns for useState, useRef, useReducer, useContext, and custom hooks.
limitations: Does not cover React Native-specific APIs.
Does not provide project-specific architecture or design system decisions.
Examples require adaptation to each framework, data layer, and authorization model.
Does not replace official React, router, or TypeScript release notes.

use_cases.title: Create Typed Components
use_cases.description: Build reusable React components with accurate props, children, refs, and variant types.

use_cases.title: Adopt React 19 Patterns
use_cases.description: Use ref as prop, useActionState, use(), Server Components, and server actions with TypeScript.

use_cases.title: Implement Typed Routing
use_cases.description: Apply type-safe route params, loader data, search params, and navigation patterns.

prompt_templates.title: Type a Basic Component
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me type a React component with TypeScript. It should extend native button props and support primary and secondary variants.

prompt_templates.title: Type Event Handlers
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my React form handlers and replace broad event types with precise TypeScript event types for inputs, submit, and keyboard actions.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Generic Component
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a generic React table component that infers column keys from the data type and supports custom render functions.

prompt_templates.title: Plan React 19 Routing
prompt_templates.prompt: Help migrate this React TypeScript feature to React 19 with Server Components, useActionState, and type-safe router loader data.

output_examples.input: I need a typed form field component for text and number inputs.
output_examples.output: The skill would suggest native input prop extension, a typed value model, precise change handlers, and accessible error identifiers.

output_examples.input: I am moving a React 18 component to React 19.
output_examples.output: The skill would identify deprecated forwardRef or useFormState usage and propose ref-as-prop and useActionState patterns.

output_examples.input: I need typed route params and search params.
output_examples.output: The skill would outline TanStack Router or React Router patterns for validated params, loader data, and navigation.

best_practices: Use specific React event types and currentTarget for element-specific typing.
Model component variants with discriminated unions instead of broad optional props.
Keep Server Components and Client Components separated by file boundary and directive.
anti_patterns: Using any for event handlers or generic render props.
Using React 19 forwardRef or deprecated useFormState in new code.
Mixing server-only APIs and client components in the same module.

faq.question: Which React versions does this skill target?
faq.answer: It covers React 18 and React 19, with explicit guidance for React 19 migration patterns.

faq.question: Does it include React Native guidance?
faq.answer: No. The skill focuses on web React with TypeScript and browser event types.

faq.question: Can it help with typed hooks?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers useState, useRef, useReducer, useContext, custom hooks, and tuple return typing.

faq.question: Does it support routing examples?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes TanStack Router and React Router v7 patterns for typed params, loaders, and search state.

faq.question: Can it generate production-ready code?
faq.answer: It provides strong TypeScript patterns, but project-specific validation, authorization, and data access still need review.

faq.question: Is this skill only for advanced users?
faq.answer: No. It includes basic component typing, intermediate event patterns, and advanced generic or routing examples.
